title: Bug: test_perf_multi_operation can exhaust ingress ACL table resources by creating two dataplane ACL tables
author: pdam-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

`generic_config_updater/test_apply_patch_perf.py::test_perf_multi_operation`  creates two ingress L3 dataplane ACL tables during setup.

  The first table is needed for the test's port-list replace operation. The
  second table is only used so the multi-op patch can remove a table.

  On platforms with limited ingress ACL table resources, creating both tables
  can exhaust dataplane ACL resources. This causes syncd/orchagent to emit
  `SAI_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`, and the test fails during teardown
  because loganalyzer catches the syslog errors.

  The test can preserve the same multi-operation coverage while consuming fewer
  dataplane ACL resources by keeping only the main table as ingress L3 and using
  a CTRLPLANE ACL table for the removable table.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the test  generic_config_updater/test_apply_patch_perf.py::test_perf_multi_operation  a broadcom ASIC Platform like x86_64-arista_7050cx3_32c

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

  **Actual behavior:**

  The test creates two ingress L3 dataplane ACL tables. On affected platforms,
  ACL table creation hits resource exhaustion. The test then fails in teardown
  because loganalyzer catches `SAI_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` messages.

  **Expected behavior:**

  The test should consume only the dataplane ACL table resources required for
  the dataplane port-list replace coverage. The removable table should not
  require another ingress dataplane ACL table if it is only used to validate
  table removal behavior.

  The test should:

  - skip cleanly when the required dataplane ACL table resource is unavailable,
  - use a CTRLPLANE ACL table for the removable table so table-remove coverage is
    preserved without consuming another dataplane ACL table.

### Relevant log output

```shell
2026 Jul 17 13:53:12.459955 gd426 ERR syncd#syncd: [none] SAI_API_ACL:_brcm_sai_xgs_field_group_create:221 field group config create failed with bcm error No resources for operation (0xfffffff2).#012!!!
  2026 Jul 17 13:53:12.459970 gd426 ERR syncd#syncd: [none] SAI_API_ACL:_brcm_sai_acl_xgs_create_table:5102 field group create failed with error -4.
  2026 Jul 17 13:53:12.459978 gd426 ERR syncd#syncd: [none] SAI_API_ACL:_brcm_sai_create_acl_table_int:837 acl create table failed with error -4.
  2026 Jul 17 13:53:12.460004 gd426 ERR syncd#syncd: :- sendApiResponse: api SAI_COMMON_API_CREATE failed in syncd mode: SAI_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES
  2026 Jul 17 13:53:12.460387 gd426 ERR syncd#syncd: :- processQuadEvent: attr: SAI_ACL_TABLE_ATTR_ACL_BIND_POINT_TYPE_LIST: 2:SAI_ACL_BIND_POINT_TYPE_PORT,SAI_ACL_BIND_POINT_TYPE_LAG
  2026 Jul 17 13:53:12.460512 gd426 ERR syncd#syncd: :- processQuadEvent: attr: SAI_ACL_TABLE_ATTR_ACL_STAGE: SAI_ACL_STAGE_INGRESS
  2026 Jul 17 13:53:12.460954 gd426 ERR swss#orchagent: :- create: create status: SAI_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES
  2026 Jul 17 13:53:12.460988 gd426 ERR swss#orchagent: :- addAclTable: Failed to create ACL table GCU_PERF_b45df4_MULTI_A
```

### Output of `show version`

```shell
platform: x86_64-arista_7050cx3_32c
hwsku: Arista-7050CX3-32C-C32
os_version: branch.202605-ars.3213bfab-buildimage.63f17ae505b85275482fef3274201014c07fed91-nightly-2026.07.15.21.40
```

> @pdam-arista — ❌ The new CRM pre-check introduces a runtime failure on multi-ASIC DUTs.
> 
> **Template**: ✅ Linked issue and 202605 failure/pass evidence provided **DCO**: ✅ Signed **CI**: ✅ Required checks are green, but they do not exercise this failing path
> 
> **Code Review:**
> 
> 1. **[Important]** `tests/generic_config_updater/test_apply_patch_perf.py:279` calls `duthost.get_crm_resources()` without an ASIC namespace. On a multi-ASIC DUT, `SonicHost.get_crm_resources()` delegates to `get_crm_resources_for_masic(namespace)`. The default namespace is `None`, while that method builds only `asic0`, `asic1`, etc. keys and returns `multi_result[namespace]`, so this call raises `KeyError: None`. This test is marked for `topology('any')`, so the change regresses multi-ASIC execution. Please query the relevant ASIC namespace(s) explicitly and add targeted multi-ASIC validation.
> 
> Please address the above before merge.

comments.author: StormLiangMS
comments.body:
Triage summary for the GCU perf failure / ADO 38693475:

This is a **sonic-mgmt test-design regression**, not a SONiC dataplane/runtime regression.

**Offending PR:** https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/24092

PR #24092 introduced `tests/generic_config_updater/test_apply_patch_perf.py` and the new `test_perf_multi_operation` coverage. During review, the removable ACL table (`table_b`) was changed from `MIRROR` to `L3` to avoid MIRROR-table conflict. That made the test create two ingress port-bound dataplane L3 ACL tables:

- `table_a`: needed for the large port-list replace perf coverage.
- `table_b`: only needed so the mixed patch can also remove one ACL table.

On Broadcom/Arista platforms with limited ingress ACL resources, allocating the second dataplane ACL table can fail with:

```text
SAI_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES
No resources for operation
addAclTable: Failed to create ACL table GCU_PERF_*
```

The test failure is then reported from teardown because LogAnalyzer catches those critical resource-exhaustion logs.

**Why this PR is the right repair:** this PR keeps the actual dataplane coverage in `table_a`, but moves the removable `table_b` to `CTRLPLANE`. That preserves the multi-operation/table-removal coverage without consuming a second ingress dataplane ACL table. The CRM pre-check also makes the test skip cleanly if the platform cannot allocate the required ingress PORT ACL table resource.

**Regression evidence:** PR #24092 merged on 2026-05-04. Kusto first shows this signature on `internal` shortly after that, then on `internal-202605` starting with `20260510.01`. The failures are concentrated on resource-limited Broadcom/Arista platforms and match the ACL table allocation error above.

**Validation:** I cherry-picked this fix to `internal-202605` and validated the target case on affected Arista hardware through Elastictest:

https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a751dcbc4dbc22bce9cf15f

Result: target `test_perf_multi_operation` passed, confirming the repair direction.

linkedPullRequests.title: tests/generic_config_updater: use CTRLPLANE table for removable table in test_perf_multi_operation
linkedPullRequests.author: MahekPatel-2403
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR

Fixes #26312

Summary:
This change updates the removable ACL table (`table_b`) in
`test_perf_multi_operation` to use a `CTRLPLANE` ACL table instead of an `L3`
ACL table.

The removable table is only created during setup and removed in the test patch.
It is never used for dataplane ACL rule operations or modified after creation.
Using a `CTRLPLANE` table preserves the purpose of the test while avoiding the
need to allocate an additional dataplane ACL table.

The primary test table (`table_a`) remains unchanged as an `L3` table with all
ports, preserving the intended leaf-list `REPLACE` performance scenario.

Fixes #26312

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Test update
- [ ] Documentation update

### How did you verify it

- Verified the file parses successfully using `python3 -m py_compile`.
- Confirmed the change is limited to `table_b`; `table_a` remains unchanged.
- Verified the `CTRLPLANE` ACL table structure matches existing patterns used in `tests/generic_config_updater/test_cacl.py`.
- Full runtime validation requires a SONiC testbed/CI environment.
